stories.headline: Delhi HC told LOC issued against CJP leader Saurav Das
stories.title: Delhi HC told LOC issued against CJP leader Saurav Das
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 26 : The Centre on Thursday informed the Delhi High Court that a Look Out Circular (LOC) had been issued against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das, who has challenged the authorities' decision to prevent him from travelling to London to attend an event at the University of Oxford. Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Chetan Sharma, appearing for the Centre, told a single-judge Bench of Justice Amit Mahajan that discrepancies detected in Das's passport could also have implications for his Indian citizenship. The Centre’s law officer submitted that the discrepancies in the passport were being examined by the authorities and that an LOC had been issued against the activist. However, senior advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for Das, told the High Court that he had not been informed about the issuance of any LOC against him. The submissions came during the hearing of Das's plea challenging the action of the authorities in stopping him at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport when he was scheduled to travel to London. The development comes a day after the Delhi High Court declined to entertain an urgent mentioning of the matter before Acting Chief Justice (ACJ) Nitin Wasudeo Sambre. Das's counsel had sought an immediate hearing, submitting that his flight to the United Kingdom was scheduled for Thursday evening and that the petition could become infructuous if not taken up urgently. The counsel had told the High Court that Das was stopped at immigration, but no order or LOC restricting his overseas travel was shown to him. However, the Acting Chief Justice declined the request for an urgent hearing on Wednesday and said the matter would be taken up on Thursday. Meanwhile, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) had said on Wednesday that the Regional Passport Office (RPO) in Chennai issued a show-cause notice to Das on November 23, seeking clarification regarding his place of birth. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, during a bi-weekly media briefing, said Das had also been advised not to use his passport until he submitted his response to the notice. Jaiswal said that a show-cause notice is issued when authorities detect discrepancies in a passport application and seek an explanation from the applicant. The controversy erupted after Das claimed on social media that he had been stopped at the Delhi airport from travelling to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford. However, the Delhi BJP disputed his version, maintaining that Das was scheduled to attend an event organised by the Oxford Union and not deliver a lecture at the university. The party also claimed that he had independently paid for registration for the event. ( IANS)

opening: India's latest move to keep Pakistani-origin content off streaming platforms, amid the huge ongoing row over Netflix's upcoming series Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo, has brought into sharp focus the enduring popularity of Pakistani dramas among Indian viewers.

The move is a continuation of the strictures that India had placed on its relations with its neighbour and arch-rival after the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor (April-May 2025), and the brief but intense military face-off that followed.

After the war, the Information and Broadcasting Ministry had on May 8, 2025 directed streaming platforms and digital intermediaries to not air Pakistani films, series, songs, podcasts and other content in India.
The directive came amid complaints over the possible December 4 India release of the series that stars Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan and Sanam Saeed.
The issue is no longer just about the entertainment industry.
On both sides of the border, there currently is a trend of seeing any kind of exchange against the backdrop of cross-border terrorism and national security.
It may be noted that Pakistan steadfastly rejects India's accusations on terrorism despite an abundance of proof.
The contrast in storytelling.
The appeal of Pakistani content for Indians lies in an assortment of factors.

Familiar language, everyday family drama, emotional storytelling and compact, easy-to-follow stories -- these characteristics have helped Pakistani productions find huge viewership in India despite the bitterness that pervades bilateral ties.
The popularity of Pakistani serials in India -- despite there being no official distribution channels -- is rooted partly in what viewers see as a contrast in storytelling.
Analysts say Pakistani content offers something that many Indian viewers feel is missing from mainstream Indian television: realism, restraint and emotional depth.

Pakistani dramas, in contrast, largely use real homes, understated production, natural dialogue and tighter story arcs; they often revolve around marriage, family expectations, heartbreak, social pressures and women's choices, it adds.
Instant pull.
These subjects resonate across the border as they don't need viewers to understand a different cultural setting, the report notes.
Urdu, the language of Pakistani content, is readily understood by much of the Hindi-speaking audience.
Besides, shared customs, food, family settings, jokes and wedding traditions make the characters recognisable.
According to a ToI report, Pakistani shows such as Humsafar, Zindagi Gulzar Hai, Kabhi Main Kabhi Tum and Mere Humsafar have developed audiences through relatable characters rather than spectacle.
Also, the episode count for Pakistani serials is usually much smaller compared to Indian ones.
That also has a role in boosting their appeal, as they let viewers follow a story arc without committing to months and months -- sometimes years -- of watching.
Small screens, big viewsIndian entertainment industry is film-dominated.
Films here are often built around theatrical releases, stars, music, big budgets and nationwide marketing.
Pakistani entertainment, on the other hand, is strongly anchored in television drama.
In Pakistan, serials have a place in popular culture, in the same manner that Bollywood has in India.
Actors become household names, weekly episodes fuel conversations and hit shows can travel way beyond their domestic audience.
India has massive scale and genre diversity, much more than its neighbour has.
Pakistani dramas have still carved out a niche for themselves through more intimate storytelling, strong writing and "performances that feel less manufactured", an AP report says.
Today's digital ecosystem has amplified this popularity even more.
YouTube uploads, short clips, Instagram reels, fan edits, character discussions and viral dialogues frequently introduce viewers to shows they might otherwise never discover.
Pakistani dramas have also garnered extraordinary global online viewership numbers.
Tere Bin has crossed 4 billion YouTube views, while Khuda Aur Mohabbat Season 3 has recorded 3 billion, ET reported.
One may note that these are worldwide figures, not India-specific viewership numbers.
Broadcasters and streaming platforms have not publicly disclosed reliable India-only audience estimates.
Content caught in crossfireTensions in India-Pakistan ties frequently seep into other areas.
Culture & entertainment often gets caught in this crossfire.
Following the 2016 Uri attack, film bodies and political groups demanded Pakistani artistes leave India.
Artists who faced flak included actors Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan, and singers Atif Aslam and Rahat Fateh Ali Khan.
After Pahalgam, Instagram accounts of several Pakistani celebs -- Fawad, Mahira, Hania Aamir and Ali Zafar -- became inaccessible in India.
Restrictions have at times extended beyond films and streaming to concerts, social-media access and professional collaborations as well, PTI reported.
India's latest reminder to Netflix was slammed in Pakistan as an attempt to politicise culture.
The most vocal among critics was Minister Ahsan Iqbal, who said artistic exchanges should not be treated as political threats.
Exclusion from Indian audiences will hurt Pakistani creators and streaming players, various reports said citing industry insiders.

stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 26: The Supreme Court on Thursday said it will consider who qualifies to be a journalist and whether accredited media persons should enjoy greater protection than self-proclaimed reporters while covering protests. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that journalistic freedom has to be balanced with the administration of public order and law. The top court relegated to the high-powered committee headed by former top court judge R Subhash Reddy to examine pleas over the alleged detention of seven journalists, assault, and obstruction of journalists covering protests in Delhi on 10 and 11 October 2026. It asked the petitioners to submit material before the five-member committee. "You will go back to the committee which we have constituted to factually demonstrate whether your petitioners were, in fact, present there. If present, whether they were subjected to excessive force. "Whether they were subjected to force and, if subjected, whether such force was excessive in relation to the proportion necessary for maintenance of public order," Justice Bagchi observed. Self-proclaimed journalists may not have the same protection as accredited journalists, he then added. The Kerala Union of Working Journalists and the Delhi Union of Journalists, in their plea, submitted that journalists were forcibly removed from reporting sites, prevented from recording events, and subjected to physical force. According to the plea, accredited journalists documenting the protests were restrained, dragged away, manhandled and detained despite displaying their press credentials. Senior advocate PV Dinesh said seven journalists working with established organisations, not reel-makers, were taken into custody. "The question is, when established journalists, who are recognised journalists, are covering events, can they be taken into custody?" the lawyer submitted. The Delhi Police earlier told the top court that social media "reel-makers" and influencers cannot claim the same protections as journalists covering protests. In an affidavit, the city police submitted that journalists "constitute a distinct category" from social media content creators who use cameras and microphones to make reels for commercial gain, arguing that the latter cannot automatically claim the protections afforded to the press while covering protests.

Addressing the Supreme Court's Constitution Day celebrations, the CJI said the Constitution was conceived not as a charter of advantages for a fortunate few, but as a covenant of justice with every citizen.

Recalling the words of Constituent Assembly member Mithi Hansa Mehta, who had said that women sought social, economic and political justice rather than privileges, the CJI said that the distinction between privilege and justice lay at the heart of the Constitution.
He likened the Supreme Court's jurisprudence to a Pashmina shawl, saying that thousands of judgments, patiently laid together, had helped shelter the Republic.
However, he pointed out that even a precious shawl could protect only those who could afford to wrap it around themselves.
Thus, he said, the Court must reflect on whether justice had reached everyone it was intended for.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) allowed the listing of a contempt petition on November 27 seeking a personal affidavit from the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary detailing the government’s decision-making, including any role played by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in the failure to light the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon on the Thirupparankundram Hill summit in compliance with the November 20 order of the court.

The petition filed by Rama Ravikumar was orally mentioned before a Bench headed by Justice Arvind Kumar at 2 p.m. The petition, settled by senior advocate P. Valliappan and filed by advocate G. Balaji, also sought the immediate preservation and production of all physical and electronic records relating to the implementation of the November 20 order.
It has made both Tamil Nadu authorities and the temple administration parties in the contempt case.
Other documents sought to include the November 23 prohibitory order and the resolution of the Board of Trustees, including the opinions purportedly obtained from the Agama experts and Sthanikars.
The petition said the court must initiate suo motu criminal contempt proceedings.

The plea also urged the apex court to invoke its plenary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution for lighting the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon in Thirupparankundram Hill on a substituted date within seven days, preferably during the current Tamil month of Karthigai, subject to the safeguards prescribed in the November 20 order, and under the personal supervision of the State Chief Secretary, with the assistance of an independent Court Commissioner and the Central Reserve.
Police Force.

The Hindu parties are seeking contempt action despite Mr. Krishna’s preliminary report of November 25, which stated that the district authorities had made all arrangements to facilitate the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon in compliance with the November 20 order.
However, the Board of Trustees at the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple had not authorised persons for the lamp-lighting team on November 24.

Another contempt plea, drawn by advocate Yashika Anand and filed through advocate Narender Kumar Verma, said the non-compliance with the apex court order of November 20 to light the lamp on November 24 at the Deepathoon as a “limited one-time arrangement” only for this year was not only contumacious but also a patent violation of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution.

article_sentences: Chennai: Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran on Thursday urged Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar to order a thorough enquiry into the alleged violations of religious rights and disregard by the state government to the Supreme Court's directive on Karthigai Deepam festival at Thirupparankundram.

Also, he requested the governor to initiate appropriate legal action against the government officials and authorities responsible for not lighting the ceremonial lamp at the stone pillar atop the Thirupparankundram hill in Madurai.
The BJP leader called on Arlekar at Lok Bhavan here and submitted a memorandum condemning the state government over the Thirupparankundram Karthigai Deepam issue and alleged police repression.

The latest developments follow the Supreme Court's November 20 order permitting the lighting of the lamp at the stone pillar atop the Thirupparankundram hill, on November 24 as a one-time measure.

After lighting the Karthigai Deepam only at the customary location atop the Thirupparankundram hill, the temple's Board of Trustees had, in a statement, asserted that long-standing religious traditions must take precedence.
The BJP leader also strongly condemned the police department's handling of the public during the episode.

In a statement, he said citizens who voiced support for their rights and demanded the implementation of the court order were treated "inhumanely" by police personnel, infringing upon their democratic rights.

Calling the actions "anti-democratic," Nagenthran urged the governor to order a thorough enquiry into the alleged violations of religious rights and initiate appropriate legal action against the government officials and authorities responsible.

Reiterating that upholding the dignity of the judiciary and protecting constitutional rights remain the party's firm duty, Nagenthran announced that the BJP's democratic protests would continue until justice is served in the matter.
Nagenthran expressed doubt about the authenticity of the police officers present at Thirupparankundram, noting that they did not wear their name plates.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Restores Compensation To Woman Who Lost Hand In Electrocution
stories.title: Supreme Court Restores Compensation To Woman Who Lost Hand In Electrocution

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has held that an appellate court cannot overturn a civil court's findings merely based on suspicion, without properly assessing the evidence and credibility of witnesses.
The Court observed that “a civil suit should be decided on the basis of evidence produced by the parties and not by merely raising a doubt on the claim made by the plaintiff.”

A bench of Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra and Justice Shree Chandrashekhar heard the case where the civil court's decision to grant compensation to the Appellant for the injury suffered by her due to electrocution was interfered with by the High Court by raising suspicion over the Appellant's case, despite her claim being supported by the witnesses and medical report.
The incident occurred on July 15, 2011, when Rekha was a minor.
She claimed that electricity wires in her village were hanging dangerously close to the ground and that she suffered injuries after coming into contact with one of them.
She lost her right hand which had to be amputated after the injury.
While the trial court accepted her claim and awarded her compensation of Rs.

8,70,000/-, the High Court reversed the decree, questioning the circumstances of the incident, the possibility of surviving contact with an 11 KV wire, inconsistencies in witness accounts and the delay in reporting the incident.
Disagreeing with the High Court's decision, the judgment authored by Justice Chandrashekhar held that the High Court had interfered with the trial court's findings on mere suspicion / ipse dixit.
It noted that Rekha's witnesses had supported her account, whereas JVVNL's witness was neither present at the incident nor on duty that day.
The respondents had also failed to produce evidence showing that the transmission lines were properly maintained.
The Court clarified that the standard of proof in civil cases is preponderance of probabilities, and not proof beyond reasonable doubt.

stories.headline: 8th Colombo Security Conclave: India, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Mauritius adopt CSC cooperation roadmap
stories.title: 8th Colombo Security Conclave: India, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Mauritius adopt CSC cooperation roadmap
stories.summary: Male, Nov 26: The 8th National Security Advisor (NSA)-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave (CSC), hosted by the Maldives on November 25, reaffirmed the commitment of member states to strengthening regional peace and security through sustained cooperation. The meeting was held at Villa Nautica Paradise Island in the Maldives, with high-level delegations led by National Security Adviser of the Maldives Ibrahim Latheef; India's National Security Adviser Ajit Doval; Secretary, Ministry of Defence, Sri Lanka, Air Vice Marshal Sampath Thuyacontha; and Commandant, National Defence College, Bangladesh, Lieutenant General Md Faizur Rahman. Australia and Malaysia participated in the meeting as guests. Australia was represented by Sarah Storey, First Assistant Secretary, South and Southeast Asia Group and Head of the Office of Southeast Asia in the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, while Malaysia was represented by Khairul Azhar (Nik) bin Abu Bakar, Director, Maritime Security and Sovereignty Division, National Security Council, Prime Minister's Department. During the meeting, the first Secretary General of the Colombo Security Conclave, Vice Admiral S N Ghormade (Retd.), presented a comprehensive review of the actions undertaken to implement the decisions of the 7th NSA-level meeting held in New Delhi on November 20, 2025. Member states, including the Maldives, India, Mauritius (virtually) and Sri Lanka, signed the Agreed Minutes and adopted the Roadmap of Cooperation for 2026–2027, outlining key deliverables and planned activities under the five pillars of cooperation. These pillars include Maritime Safety and Security; Countering Terrorism and Radicalisation; Combating Trafficking and Transnational Organised Crime; Cyber Security and Protection of Critical Infrastructure and Technology; and Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief. The meeting reaffirmed the collective commitment of member states to promoting regional peace and security through sustained cooperation. Emphasis was placed on strengthening collaboration across the five pillars, particularly through training, sharing of best practices and capacity-building initiatives, while underscoring the importance of continued collective efforts to advance the objectives of the Colombo Security Conclave.

stories.headline: Indian exporters urge early US trade deal, cite proposed 17% tariff advantage
stories.title: Indian exporters urge early US trade deal, cite proposed 17% tariff advantage
stories.summary: With US orders picking up, exporters say an early agreement would help Indian businesses protect competitiveness and secure greater market access
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Indian exporters on Thursday urged the government to seal a trade pact with the US at the earliest, saying the proposed 17 per cent tariff, as outlined in the USTR report, would give India an advantage over competing nations.
They said that this is the right time to finalise the deal as exporters are getting good orders from the US buyers.
“India should do the trade deal as soon as possible.
We are getting a lot of orders from the US, and further opening of the market will help increase exports,” Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) President S C Ralhan said.

He added that the absence of a trade deal with the US could hurt India’s exports by putting domestic exporters at a disadvantage compared with competitors from countries that enjoy lower tariff rates.
This could affect the price competitiveness of Indian goods in the US market, making it difficult for exporters to retain existing buyers and secure new orders, Ralhan said.

He added that the agreement should be balanced and reciprocal, safeguard India’s long-term economic and developmental interests, and ensure that Indian exporters can compete on a level playing field with suppliers from other countries in the US market.
“While the industry is concerned with these developments as it raises uncertainty, there is no panic amongst exporters,” he said.
Ralhan also called for clarity on how the proposed measures would interact with existing duties under Sections 301 and 232 and how the product-specific exemptions in the USTR notice would apply.
“Clear rules on the duties payable on each product would help exporters quote prices with confidence and avoid overlapping tariff burdens,” he said.
FIEO urged negotiators to secure competitive tariff treatment for Indian products, address non-tariff barriers and improve market access.
It called for particular attention to MSMEs, which have less room to absorb sudden increases in duties and compliance costs.
